text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — High 429/latency on inference endpoints (chat+embeddings+rerrank). 5xx low but throttles spiking. P95 latency on /v1/chat up from 120ms -> 450ms. Error rate (429) increased from 0.2% -> 8% in last 6m. Rolling window: 2023-08-14T12:34:49Z. Pager: kevin (oncall)

kevin (oncall): ack, I'm oncall. grabbing logs now. any customer-facing spikes? pinging support.

jess (support): seeing ~60 customer reports over the last 10m — mostly embedding requests returning 429s and some rerank timeouts. Biggest noisy customer: corp-acme (heavy embedding batch jobs).

alex (sre): quick gut check — metrics show a huge burst from /v1/embeddings (client keys: many small keys from corp-acme + anonymous). Token generation looks normal. Looks like a sudden increase in concurrent embedding streams causing KV cache pressure and queue backs. Chat latency rising due to head-of-line blocking.

maria (pm): customer impact severity? any paid customers affected (Dedicated/Private)?

jess (support): corp-acme (paid) seeing 429s on embeddings batch endpoint. A few smaller free-tier users also hit rerank 429s.

kevin (oncall): plan: targeted per-route throttles to protect chat first, then throttle embeddings noisy keys and disable rerank for free-tier. We should avoid global rate limit rollback. Want to apply route-specific quotas and then re-evaluate in 2m. @alex can you run the quota tweaks?

alex (sre): on it. running playbook "route-shaping: embeddings-first". steps: 1) apply per-route limit on /v1/embeddings 2) add customer-scoped limit for corp-acme with backoff 3) disable rerank for free-tier 4) validate dashes

alex (sre): running admin commands now — pasting commands I'm using:

```
# limit global embeddings to 1200rpm to shed bursty traffic
redwood-admin quotas update --route "/v1/embeddings" --limit 1200rpm --scope global --reason "mitigation: burst"

# apply customer-specific cap for corp-acme to 500rpm
redwood-admin quotas update --route "/v1/embeddings" --limit 500rpm --scope client:corp-acme --reason "noisy-client throttle"

# disable rerank for free tier users (soft-disable: 429 with retry-after)
redwood-admin feature-toggle set --feature rerank --state partial_disable --scope free-tier --reason "mitigation"
```

ops-bot: ACTION: quotas.update request received. id=quo-9f3b. Target /v1/embeddings global -> 1200rpm.

ops-bot: ACTION: quotas.update request received. id=quo-9f3c. Target /v1/embeddings client:corp-acme -> 500rpm.

ops-bot: ACTION: feature-toggle request received. id=ft-22b. Target rerank free-tier -> partial_disable.

ops-bot: SUCCESS: quo-9f3b applied (200). new global embeddings limit=1200rpm.

ops-bot: SUCCESS: quo-9f3c applied (200). corp-acme embeddings cap=500rpm.

ops-bot: SUCCESS: ft-22b applied (200). rerank responses now return 429+Retry-After for free-tier.

alex (sre): monitoring post-change. queue depth for embeddings down ~68% in 45s. P95 chat latency dropping from 450ms -> 180ms. 429 rate overall down from 8% -> 2.1%. good immediate improvement but corp-acme still seeing occasional spikes (they're right at 500rpm).

jess (support): notifying corp-acme about temporary cap + mitigation link: https://redwood.internal/status/inc-2034506789. will send template: "we applied temporary quota to smooth platform traffic; we'll update you before we roll back." :email:

maria (pm): are there any customers that will be blocked by disabling rerank? can we whitelist enterprise customers?

alex (sre): rerank partial_disable was scoped to free-tier. enterprise and dedicated unaffected. leaving as-is for now.

kevin (oncall): next steps: 1) keep route-specific limits for 15m, 2) watch for regressions, 3) if corp-acme remains noisy, propose scheduled maintenance or ask them to batch jobs. I'll hand off to alex after 20m for further follow-up.

jess (support): corp-acme acknowledges. asked for ETA on rollback.

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE — 2034506920: embeddings qDepth -68%, p95_chat 180ms, overall 429 -> 2.1%

alex (sre): minor tweak — added per-api-key leaky bucket for anonymous keys to 20rpm to stop bursty auto-scaling tests from free clients:

```
redwood-admin quotas update --route "/v1/embeddings" --limit 20rpm --scope key_prefix:anon_ --reason "stop burst tests"
```

ops-bot: SUCCESS: quo-9f4a applied (200). anon_ keys capped.

alex (sre): after anonymous cap, tail latency improved and queues stabilized. corp-acme still at cap but not saturating backend now.

kevin (oncall): nice. prepping handoff. I'm going to log timeline and start incident doc. alex you'll take L2 follow-up, maria owns customer comms, jess keep monitoring support queue.

maria (pm): assigning postmortem owner: maria. include: root cause, why noisy traffic wasn't auto-throttled sooner, why rerank contributed to head-of-line blocking, and recommendations (better default per-route guards, early noisy-client detection).

alex (sre): action item: add automated rule in routing layer to deprioritize embeddings spikes and protect chat within 5s of p95>250ms. I'll open PR after incident.

jess (support): customers updated. creating CX ticket for corp-acme with mitigation steps and ask them to reschedule nightly batch to off-peak window.

kevin (oncall): handing off to alex in 18m. if anything spikes, page alex. I'm logging the incident in incidents board now. thanks team. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: HANDOFF logged: from kevin to alex. incident state=mitigated, ticket=INC-2034506789.

alex (sre): acknowledged handoff. I'll keep a 1h watch and then escalate to infra if flapping.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status=mitigated -> monitoring. will auto-close if stable for 30m.

kevin (oncall): out.

jess (support): closing immediate customer alerts, leaving open tickets for follow-up.

maria (pm): added follow-up items to backlog: route-specific default quotas, noisy-client auto-detection, better observability for rerank queueing.

alex (sre): created PR for monitoring rule and runbook edits. will include CLI snippets and exact quota values we used.

ops-bot: NOTE: audit log created for quota changes: quo-9f3b, quo-9f3c, quo-9f4a.

incident-bot: THREAD TIMELINE: created=2034506789 last_update=2034507110
